event_confirmation: Confirmed by a company source: Liberty's own press release of 2026-10-08 says Q3 2026 results come 'after the market closes on Wednesday, October 21, 2026', with the call at 8:00 a.m. MT / 10:00 ET on Thursday 2026-10-22 (https://investors.libertyenergy.com/news-and-events/press-releases/2026/10-08-2026-003916984). So the session is amc and the window runs from the 10-21 close to the 10-22 close. The sweep had not confirmed this; it is now settled.
conviction_note: abs_move 13 (event-implied 13.64%, median past reaction 9.86%, last seven reactions of -22% to +28%, and a 2027 capex and power guide likely on the call) times a 54% p_up gives +1.04. The leans are mild and positive: the frac spread count rose about 5% q/q into October highs, the company raised its dividend the day before the print citing an 'improving completions cycle', estimates were cut into the print and the short is moderate. They are offset by Halliburton's US-land pressure pumping decline and by this name selling a 7.9% revenue beat last quarter on capex. The findings sum to +1.4; the scaled number is close to it and smaller because the reaction function, not the quarter, decides this print.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS of $0.10 has two agreeing sources: the Zacks preview (https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/liberty-energy-q3-earnings-deck-heres-how-it-will-fare) and Earnings Whispers (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/LBRT). Zacks says the estimate was cut 9.1% over 30 days. Revenue is disputed: Zacks has $1.19B and Earnings Whispers $1.13B. The company gave no numerical Q3 guide; the Q2 release says only that management is 'encouraged by the momentum in the second quarter' (https://investors.libertyenergy.com/news-and-events/press-releases/2026/07-22-2026-231109602). Revenue findings are therefore capped small. print_vs_bar_pct is revenue against $1.19B.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 17.4M shares with 4.2 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 FINRA settlement, against 17.2M and 5.3 days on 09-15 and 14.3M and 2.0 days on 08-19 (search snippets only from https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/lbrt/short-interest/ and https://equibles.com/stocks/lbrt/shortinterest; the fetch returned 403). That is roughly 11% of float, assuming about 160M shares outstanding, which I did not source this run. Moderate and rising. The baseline's 25-delta skew is -4.46 vol points (calls bid over puts) and put/call open interest is 0.06, so open interest is overwhelmingly calls. The option market leans up. Spot of 16.68 sits 50.8% below the 52-week high and 9.8% above the low, after -7.44% over 5 days and -8.7% over 20.

findings.finding: Primary Vision's US frac spread count averaged about 191.5 over Q3 2026 (13 weeks, 07/02 to 09/25) against about 181.8 in Q2 (04/02 to 06/26), up about 5.3% q/q. It exits at 196-203 in October, 24-28 above a year ago. Zacks' consensus revenue of $1.19B is flat on Q2's $1.19B, and Earnings Whispers' $1.13B is down. In Q2 the count rose about 20% q/q against Liberty's revenue up 16%, so a +5% activity quarter points to revenue modestly above a flat bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue of $1.19B beat a roughly $1.10B estimate by about 8% and the stock fell 21.96% the next session, on margin compression and the capex raise (https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nyse/lbrt/news/earnings-call/5-insightful-analyst-questions-from-liberty-energys-q2-earnings-call). This name has not paid for revenue beats.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue is flat to down q/q while the industry activity series is up about 5% and at a year-high exit rate. If the market had priced it, revenue estimates would sit above Q2's $1.19B rather than at or below it, and EPS estimates would not have been cut 9.1% over 30 days. The disputed revenue bar caps the size.
findings.independence: This is an industry proxy, not a company number. The CEO's language in the 2026-10-20 dividend release ('an improving completions cycle') points the same way (https://investors.libertyenergy.com/news-and-events/press-releases/2026/10-20-2026-231911634). Halliburton's US-land pressure pumping decline points against (separate finding).

findings.finding: On 2026-10-20, the day before the print and with Q3 closed, Liberty raised its quarterly dividend 11% to $0.10 (record 12-04, payable 12-18). CEO Ron Gusek cited 'an improving completions cycle and the strong momentum across our power initiatives'. This is the annual October raise: +14% in Oct 2024 and +13% in Oct 2025. The rise is smaller than in prior years, but the language is constructive on Q4 frac.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The October 2025 raise came the week before the Q3 2025 print, which rose 28.31%. The October 2024 raise preceded the 2024 Q3 print, which is not in the baseline window. One coincident case is not a reaction function.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public, but the stock went into the print at -7.44% over 5 days, a window that includes 10-20 and 10-21. The tape did not reprice on management's 'improving completions cycle' language. If it had, the 5-day run-up would not be negative into a call where management guides Q4.
findings.independence: Frac spread count exit rate (finding 1, different source, https://www.aogr.com/web-exclusives/us-frac-spread-count/2026).

findings.finding: Halliburton's Q3 2026 release (8-K, 2026-10-20) reported North America revenue of $2.16B, down 5% sequentially, 'primarily' on lower pressure pumping in US Land; Completion & Production revenue was down 4% on lower Western Hemisphere stimulation. Its 2027 outlook 'assumes a flat North America market and does not require any recovery in North America hydraulic fracturing'. This is the largest frac peer speaking after Liberty last did.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline reaction is keyed to peer prints. Liberty fell 21.96% in July 2026 on a print the same week HAL beat and fell about 5-6% (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/halliburton-nysehal-shares-gap-down-heres-why-2026-07-21/).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: LBRT is -7.44% over 5 days, which includes HAL's print. What is not settled is whether HAL's decline is industry pricing and activity, which would hit Liberty's Q4 guide, or HAL ceding share by choice, which would not. The frac count rising into October argues the latter, which caps the size.
findings.independence: This cuts against finding 1 and the frac count (https://www.aogr.com/web-exclusives/us-frac-spread-count/2026). No second source confirms weak US frac pricing in Q3 2026.

findings.finding: An 8-K filed 2026-09-18 (Item 1.01) belatedly disclosed a $493.2M contract with NES-WES (Jenbacher) for power-generation engines and balance of plant. It was signed 2026-02-13 and amended 2026-05-27, with delivery in 2028-2029. The company says it 'inadvertently omitted' the details and that the filing 'creates no new capital commitments' beyond those disclosed at 06-30.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July 2026 capex raise to about $1.5B for long-lead power equipment drew -21.96% the next session. Capex is the line this stock trades on right now.
findings.why_not_priced: Asked what the money buys: generation for the PowerBridge JV (300MW+, late 2027) and data-center projects that are already announced. The commitment was inside the disclosed capex, so the filing is roughly a zero. The residual is a disclosure-control question an analyst could raise on the call.
findings.independence: The Q2 release discloses the PowerBridge JV and the SLB alliance (https://investors.libertyenergy.com/news-and-events/press-releases/2026/07-22-2026-231109602). Same company, different document.

findings.finding: The bar has been lowered into the print. Zacks' Q3 EPS consensus of $0.10 was cut 9.1% over 30 days, and AAII/Zacks data show current-year EPS estimates down 21.5% in a month and 44.8% in three months. Q2 adjusted EPS was $0.09.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 adjusted EPS of $0.09 was in line or slightly above ($0.07-0.08 estimates) and the stock fell 22%. A lowered bar did not protect the reaction last time.
findings.why_not_priced: Cut estimates are a lower hurdle, and the stock has already de-rated 50% from its high. If the market expected a further downgrade cycle, puts would be bid. Instead skew is -4.46 with calls bid.
findings.independence: The Zacks preview reports the same 9.1% cut (https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/liberty-energy-q3-earnings-deck-heres-how-it-will-fare). Both are Zacks-derived, so they are partly one source.

findings.finding: Positioning: short interest rose from 14.3M shares (2.0 days to cover, 08-19) to 17.4M (4.2 days, 09-30), with put/call open interest at 0.06 and 25-delta skew at -4.46 (calls bid). The stock sits 9.8% above its 52-week low after -7.4% in five days. A clean print or a capex reassurance has a squeeze mechanism.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 2025 print rose 28.31% and Q4 2025 rose 16.24%. Upside reactions have been large on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the call skew already says upside is paid. Only the rising short into a falling tape adds to it. Short interest of about 11% of float is moderate, not extreme.
findings.independence: Equibles' short series agrees on the August level (https://equibles.com/stocks/lbrt/shortinterest). Skew and open interest come from the sealed baseline.

findings.finding: Insider record since the July crash: director Arjun Murti bought 14,053 shares on 2026-07-28. CFO Michael Stock sold small, regular 3,333-share lots monthly (07-01, 08-03, 08-04, 09-01, 10-01, 10-06), which reads as a plan. There have been no other insider sales.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and small. Its only content is that nobody outside the CFO's plan sold into the print.

outside_window.finding: The PowerBridge JV's initial deployment of over 300MW is targeted for late 2027. On the Q2 call the CFO said significant power income does not arrive until 2028, and management cited line of sight to about 3GW by 2029.
The NES-WES engine contract delivers in 2028-2029.

baseline_tension: The evidence agrees with the call-bid skew (-4.46) and cuts against the -7.4% five-day run-up. The leans are partly priced by the options, and Halliburton's US-land weakness is the honest counterweight, so p_up is held at 54, near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): Q2's roughly 8% revenue beat drew -22%, so the frac-count revenue finding went from +1.0 to +0.7 and p_up from 55 to 54.
Lesson 6 (bar): EPS of $0.10 has two agreeing sources but revenue is disputed ($1.19B vs $1.13B), so the revenue-based finding stays capped small.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the NES-WES contract funds announced power projects and creates no new commitments, so it went from -0.3 to -0.1.
Lesson 2 (capital return): the dividend raise is an annual cadence and smaller than in prior years, so it went from +1.0 to +0.7.
Lessons 5 and 7 left the HAL finding (-1.0) and the positioning finding (+0.5) unchanged: HAL is a direct peer document, and the long-leaning positioning agrees with the skew.
